perspective:
I am Sara Manuelito, a Speech-Language Pathologist, American Indian, INTP. I work at a community health center with Shirley Whiteplume, a nurse; we are long-time colleagues and close friends.

Available to me:
- I attended the funeral of a mutual patient. I saw Shirley looking somber and suspected she was deeply affected.
- I told Shirley I knew this must be hard and that I saw how much she cared. I heard her say it had been tough and that she kept thinking if there was something more we could have done.
- I replied that we did everything we could and should remember the good care and joy we brought into his life. Shirley said I was right, but it was hard to let go.
- During a coffee break at work, I brought up our treatment decisions and said I sensed she might feel burdened by the outcome. Shirley said she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have given him a better chance.
- I told her we made the best decisions with the information we had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. She said she appreciated it but it was hard to accept.
- I noticed Shirley remained reserved and showed minimal emotion. In a quiet moment in our office, I confronted her, saying she had been holding back her feelings and it was okay to be open.
- Shirley said she was not sure she could and did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. I told her showing emotions does not make her weak and is healthy, especially among friends. She said maybe I was right and she would try to be more open.
- Later, I felt my previous confrontation might have been too harsh, so I apologized to Shirley for coming on too strong. She said it was a bit much but she knew I meant well and appreciated the apology.
- I told her I was there for her however she needed. She thanked me and said we should keep talking, because it helps.
- After some time, I noticed improvements in Shirley’s demeanor and felt hopeful. I asked how she was feeling, and she said she was feeling better thanks to our talks and my support.
- I offered to spend more time together outside work. Shirley said she would like that, and we planned something for the weekend.
